## I CASE MANAGEMENT

## The court’s general powers of management

## 3.1

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (1) The list of powers in this rule is in addition to any powers given to the court by any other rule or practice direction or by any other enactment or any powers it may otherwise have. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (2) Except where these Rules provide otherwise, the court may –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (a) extend or shorten the time for compliance with any rule, practice direction or court order (even if an application for extension is made after the time for compliance has expired);

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (b) adjourn or bring forward a hearing;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (c) require that any proceedings in the High Court be heard by a Divisional Court of the High Court;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (d) require a party or a party’s legal representative to attend the court;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (e) hold a hearing and receive evidence by telephone or by using any other method of direct oral communication;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (f) direct that part of any proceedings (such as a counterclaim) be dealt with as separate proceedings;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (g) stay (GL) the whole or part of any proceedings or judgment either generally or until a specified date or event;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (h) consolidate proceedings;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (i) try two or more claims on the same occasion;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (j) direct a separate trial of any issue;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (k) decide the order in which issues are to be tried;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (l) exclude an issue from consideration;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (m) dismiss or give judgment on a claim after a decision on a preliminary issue;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (n) order any party to file and exchange a costs budget;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (o) order the parties to engage in alternative dispute resolution; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (p) take any other step or make any other order for the purpose of managing the case and furthering the overriding objective, including hearing an Early Neutral Evaluation with the aim of helping the parties settle the case. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (3) When the court makes an order, it may –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (a) make it subject to conditions, including a condition to pay a sum of money into court; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (b) specify the consequence of failure to comply with the order or a condition. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (3A) Where the court has made a direction in accordance with paragraph (2)(c) the proceedings shall be heard by a Divisional Court of the High Court and not by a single judge. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (4) Where the court gives directions it will take into account whether or not a party has complied with the Practice Direction (Pre-Action Conduct) and any relevant pre-action protocol (GL) . [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (5) The court may order a party to pay a sum of money into court if that party has, without good reason, failed to comply with a rule, practice direction or a relevant pre-action protocol. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (6) When exercising its power under paragraph (5) the court must have regard to –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (a) the amount in dispute; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (b) the costs which the parties have incurred or which they may incur. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (6A) Where a party pays money into court following an order under paragraph (3) or (5), the money shall be security for any sum payable by that party to any other party in the proceedings. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (7) A power of the court under these Rules to make an order includes a power to vary or revoke the order. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1] (8) The court may contact the parties from time to time in order to monitor compliance with directions. The parties must respond promptly to any such enquiries from the court. ## Case management – unrepresented parties

## 3.1A

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1A] (1) This rule applies in any proceedings where at least one party is unrepresented. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1A] (2) When the court is exercising any powers of case management, it must have regard to the fact that at least one party is unrepresented. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1A] (3) Both the parties and the court must, when drafting case management directions in the multi-track, intermediate track and fast track, take as their starting point any relevant standard directions which can be found online at www.justice.gov.uk/courts/procedure-rules/civil and adapt them as appropriate to the circumstances of the case. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1A] (4) The court must adopt such procedure at any hearing as it considers appropriate to further the overriding objective. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1A] (5) At any hearing where the court is taking evidence this may include—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1A] (a) ascertaining from an unrepresented party the matters about which the witness may be able to give evidence or on which the witness ought to be cross-examined; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.1A] (b) putting, or causing to be put, to the witness such questions as may appear to the court to be proper. ## Court officer’s power to refer to a judge

## 3.2 Where a step is to be taken by a court officer–

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.2 Where a step is to be taken by a court officer–] (a) the court officer may consult a judge before taking that step;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.2 Where a step is to be taken by a court officer–] (b) the step may be taken by a judge instead of the court officer. ## Court’s power to make order of its own initiative

## 3.3

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (1) Except where a rule or some other enactment provides otherwise, the court may exercise its powers on an application or of its own initiative. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (Part 23 sets out the procedure for making an application)

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (2) Where the court proposes to make an order of its own initiative –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (a) it may give any person likely to be affected by the order an opportunity to make representations; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (b) where it does so it must specify the time by and the manner in which the representations must be made. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (3) Where the court proposes –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (a) to make an order of its own initiative; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (b) to hold a hearing to decide whether to make the order, it must give each party likely to be affected by the order at least 3 days’ notice of the hearing. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (4) The court may make an order of its own initiative, without hearing the parties or giving them an opportunity to make representations. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (5) Where the court has made an order under paragraph (4) –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (a) a party affected by the order may apply to have it set aside (GL) , varied or stayed (GL) ; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (b) the order must contain a statement of the right to make such an application. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (6) An application under paragraph (5)(a) must be made –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (a) within such period as may be specified by the court; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (b) if the court does not specify a period, not more than 7 days after the date on which the order was served on the party making the application. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (7) An application under paragraph (5)(a) shall be considered at an oral hearing unless the court decides and states in an order that the application is totally without merit. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (8) If the court decides under paragraph (7) that the application is totally without merit, an application under paragraph (5)(a) may be made for reconsideration without an oral hearing.”; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (9) If the court of its own initiative strikes out a statement of case or dismisses an application,

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (including an application for permission to appeal or for permission to apply for judicial review) and it considers that the claim or application is totally without merit –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (a) the court’s order must record that fact; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.3] (b) the court must at the same time consider whether it is appropriate to make a civil restraint order. ## Power to strike out a statement of case

## 3.4

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (1) In this rule and rule 3.5, reference to a statement of case includes reference to part of a statement of case. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (2) The court may strike out (GL) a statement of case if it appears to the court –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (a) that the statement of case discloses no reasonable grounds for bringing or defending the claim;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (b) that the statement of case is an abuse of the court’s process or is otherwise likely to obstruct the just disposal of the proceedings;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (c) that there has been a failure to comply with a rule, practice direction or court order; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (d )that, in the case of a claimant’s statement of case—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (i) the claim is strategic litigation against public participation, being a SLAPP claim within the meaning of section 195 of the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (ii) the claimant has failed to show that it is more likely than not the claim would succeed at trial. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (Rules 20.2 and 20.3 provide that counterclaims and other additional claims are treated as claims and that references to a claimant include a party bringing an additional claim.)

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (3) When the court strikes out a statement of case it may make any consequential order it considers appropriate. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (4) Where –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (a) the court has struck out a claimant’s statement of case;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (b) the claimant has been ordered to pay costs to the defendant; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (c) before the claimant pays those costs, the claimant starts another claim against the same defendant, arising out of facts which are the same or substantially the same as those relating to the claim in which the statement of case was struck out, the court may, on the application of the defendant, stay(GL) that other claim until the costs of the first claim have been paid. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (5) Paragraph (2) does not limit any other power of the court to strike out(GL) a statement of case. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (6) If the court strikes out a claimant’s statement of case and it considers that the claim is totally without merit –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (a) the court’s order must record that fact; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (b) the court must at the same time consider whether it is appropriate to make a civil restraint order. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.4] (7) If a defendant applies to strike out all or part of the claim form or particulars of claim, that defendant need not file a defence before the hearing. ## Judgment without trial after striking out

## 3.5

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5] (1) This rule applies where –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5] (a) the court makes an order which includes a term that the statement of case of a party shall be struck out if the party does not comply with the order; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5] (b) the party against whom the order was made does not comply with it. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5] (2) A party may obtain judgment with costs by filing a request for judgment if –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5] (a) the order referred to in paragraph (1)(a) relates to the whole of a statement of case; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5] (b) where the party wishing to obtain judgment is the claimant, the claim is for –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5] (i) a specified amount of money;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5] (ii) an amount of money to be decided by the court;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5] (iii) delivery of goods where the claim form gives the defendant the alternative of paying their value; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5] (iv) any combination of these remedies. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5] (3) Where judgment is obtained under this rule in a case to which paragraph (2)(b)(iii) applies, it will be judgment requiring the defendant to deliver goods, or (if the defendant does not do so) pay the value of the goods as decided by the court (less any payments made). [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5] (4) The request must state that the right to enter judgment has arisen because the court’s order has not been complied with. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5] (5) A party must make an application in accordance with Part 23 if they wish to obtain judgment under this rule in a case to which paragraph (2) does not apply. ## Judgment without trial after striking out a claim in the Civil National Business Centre

## 3.5A

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5A] (1) If a claimant files a request for judgment in the Civil National Business Centre in accordance with rule 3.5, in a claim which includes an amount of money to be decided by the court, the claim will be sent to the preferred hearing centre. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.5A] (2) If a claim is sent to a preferred hearing centre pursuant to paragraph (1), any further correspondence should be sent to, and any further requests should be made at, the hearing centre to which the claim was sent. ## Setting aside judgment entered after striking out

## 3.6

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.6] (1) A party against whom the court has entered judgment under rule 3.5 may apply to the court to set the judgment aside. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.6] (2) An application under paragraph (1) must be made not more than 14 days after the judgment has been served on the party making the application. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.6] (3) If the right to enter judgment had not arisen at the time when judgment was entered, the court must set aside (GL) the judgment. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.6] (4) If the application to set aside (GL) is made for any other reason, rule 3.9 (relief from sanctions) shall apply. ## 3.6A If—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.6A If—] (a) a party against whom judgment has been entered under rule 3.5 applies to set the judgment aside;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.6A If—] (b) the claim is for a specified sum;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.6A If—] (c) the claim was started in the Civil National Business Centre; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.6A If—] (d) the claim has not been sent to a County Court hearing centre,

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.6A If—] the claim will be sent to—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.6A If—] (i) if the defendant is an individual, the defendant’s home court; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.6A If—] (ii) if the defendant is not an individual, the preferred hearing centre. ## Sanctions for non-payment of certain fees by the claimant

## 3.7

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (1) Except where rule 3.7A1 applies, this rule applies to fees payable by the claimant where—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (a) omitted;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (b) omitted;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (c) omitted;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (d) the court has made an order giving permission to proceed with a claim for judicial review; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (e) the fee payable for a hearing specified by the Civil Proceedings Fees Order 2008 1 (Fees Order 2008) is not paid. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (Rule 54.12 provides for the service of the order giving permission to proceed with a claim for judicial review)

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (2) The court will serve a notice on the claimant requiring payment of the fee specified in the Fees Order 2008 if, at the time the fee is due, the claimant has not paid it or made an application for full or part remission. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (3) The notice will specify the date by which the claimant must pay the fee. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (4) If the claimant does not –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (a) pay the fee; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (b) make an application for full or part remission of the fee, by the date specified in the notice –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (i) the claim will automatically be struck out without further order of the court; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (ii) the claimant will be liable for the costs which the defendant has incurred unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (Rule 44.9 provides for the basis of assessment where a right to costs arises under this rule and contains provisions about when a costs order is deemed to have been made and applying for an order under section 194(3) of the Legal Services Act 2007 2 )

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (5) Where an application for –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (a) full or part remission of a fee is refused, the court will serve notice on the claimant requiring payment of the full fee by the date specified in the notice; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (b) part remission of a fee is granted, the court will serve notice on the claimant requiring payment of the balance of the fee by the date specified in the notice.”; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (6) If the claimant does not pay the fee by the date specified in the notice –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (a) the claim will automatically be struck out without further order of the court; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (b) the claimant will be liable for the costs which the defendant has incurred unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (7) If –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (a) a claimant applies to have the claim reinstated; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (b) the court grants relief, the relief will be conditional on the claimant either paying the fee or filing evidence of full or part remission of the fee within the period specified in paragraph (8). [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (8) The period referred to in paragraph (7) is –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (a) if the order granting relief is made at a hearing at which the claimant is present or represented, 2 days from the date of the order;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7] (b) in any other case, 7 days from the date of service of the order on the claimant. ## Sanctions for non-payment of the trial fee by the claimant

## 3.7A1

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (1) In this rule and in rule 3.7AA—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (a ”Fees Order 2008” means the Civil Proceedings Fees Order 2008;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (b) ”fee notice” means a notice of—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (i) the amount of a trial fee;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (ii) the trial fee payment date; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (iii) the consequences of non-payment of the trial fee;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (c) “trial date” means the date of the trial in relation to which the trial fee is payable, and if the trial in relation to which the trial fee is payable is scheduled to commence during the course of a specified period, “trial date” means the date of the Monday of the first week of that specified period;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (d) “trial fee” means fee 2.1 set out in the Table in Schedule 1 to the Fees Order 2008 3 and payable for the trial of a case on the multi-track, intermediate track, fast track or small claims track;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (e) “trial fee payment date” means the date by which the trial fee must be paid, calculated in accordance with the Fees Order 2008;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (f) “revised trial fee payment date” means, if an application for fee remission is denied in whole or part, the revised date by which the fee or part of it is to be paid, calculated in accordance with the Fees Order 2008. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (2) This rule applies in relation to trial fees where that fee is to be paid by the claimant and the court notifies the parties in writing of the trial date. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (3) When the court notifies the parties in writing of the trial date, the court must also send a fee notice to the claimant. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (4) The fee notice may be contained in the same document as the notice of trial date, or may be a separate document. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (5) Where an application for full or part remission of a trial fee is refused, when the court sends written notice to the claimant of the refusal, the court must also notify the claimant in writing—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (a) that the claimant is required to pay the full trial fee by the revised trial fee payment date; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (b) of the consequences of non-payment of the trial fee. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (6) Where part remission of a fee is granted, when the court sends written notice to the claimant of the part remission, the court must also notify the claimant in writing—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (a) that the claimant is required to pay the balance of the trial fee by the revised trial fee payment date; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (b) of the consequences of non-payment of the balance of the trial fee. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (7) If—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (a) the claimant has had notice in accordance with this rule to pay the trial fee;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (b) the claimant has not applied to have the trial fee remitted in whole or part; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (c) the trial fee has not been paid on or before the trial fee payment date,

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] the claim will automatically be struck out without further order of the court, and unless the court orders otherwise, the claimant will be liable for the defendant’s costs in accordance with rule 44.9(1).
